summary: This benchmark evaluates representation steering and donor state transplantation between Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and Qwen2.5-72B across mirrored dictionary lookup prompts under two declaration orders. The evaluation is conducted on a fresh 256-group cohort with strict controls, demonstrating a substantial late-versus-early steering gain (35.77 points) and matching the full-state exchange baseline while preserving constant-table outputs.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design featuring a preregistered fresh split disjoint from the discovery cohort to prevent overfitting.
Comprehensive baseline comparisons including full-state swaps and equal-norm orthogonal negative controls.
Detailed reporting of exact runtime environment, commit hashes, peak memory usage, and hardware configuration.
Sound statistical methodology utilizing 5,000 bootstrap resamples to compute paired confidence intervals.
weaknesses: Declaration order change couples two confounding variables: prior token context and the token span between key declaration and the answer generation site.
The evaluation scope is restricted to synthetic two-key Python dictionary lookup prompts and single-token answer generation.
The paper is very concise and omits broader contextualization within the activation addition and linear representation engineering literature.
suggestions: Disentangle context ordering from response distance using matched filler tokens or prompt padding as explored in the cited follow-up.
Broaden the benchmark to evaluate multi-key dictionaries and non-numeric value mappings to test generalizability.
Include an ablation analyzing how performance scales with varying donor subspace dimensionality beyond the seven-coordinate interface.
